question.text: In the yield-curve strategy literature, a BULLET portfolio concentrates duration at:

explanation.text: The Logic: In yield-curve strategy terminology, a bullet portfolio concentrates duration around a single target maturity point (for example, a 10-year focus). A barbell, by contrast, places weight at both the short and long ends with little in the middle, and a ladder spreads positions roughly evenly across maturities. The Trap: "Both short and long ends" describes a barbell; "evenly spread" describes a ladder; "only at the shortest end" describes a cash-like or money-market-tilt strategy — none of these match the bullet structure. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook defines barbell as concentration at both ends of the duration spectrum with minimal mid-duration bonds and mentions zero-coupon bullet-payment instruments as an active strategy, but does not explicitly define a bullet portfolio as duration concentrated at a single maturity point. The bullet/barbell/ladder taxonomy above reflects general industry/fixed-income strategy terminology.
